item.title: Physician Videos
item.dc:creator: wtingen
item.content:encoded:
Physician Videos

The Challenge

When new physicians join the Tanner Health System team, part of their promotional package includes an introductory video. It is seen as a chance for patients to get a better feel for who the physicians are and how they will engage with the community they serve.

Video shots involved scouting the location, interviewing the doctor, directing the shoot (interview and b-roll) and preparing graphics for intros and outros. When physicians join Tanner they receive a promotional package which includes the video and other media such as direct mail, email, social media posts, a press release and promotion on the Tanner.org website.

Results

These videos have helped each doctor touch the community and also engage and gather new and old patients.

item.title: Tanner Health Pavilion
item.dc:creator: wtingen
item.content:encoded:
Tanner Health Pavilion

The Challenge

As the Tanner Health Pavilion was being constructed, we were asked to provide branding and strategy guidance. The challenge was to maintain aspects of the Tanner Health System brand yet introduce some modern design. The resulting logo and branding were to be used on both the exterior and interior of the building.

The open house and other promotional materials introduced the pavilion brand.

An additional challenge within the facility was the bistro. It was to have its own standalone brand. Because of the proximity to the local community walking and biking trail, The Carrollton GreenBelt, leadership named it Blue Bike Bistro. This logo was required to have more freedom and flowing lines than that of the pavilion.

Results

Tanner Health Pavilion has become a center point of the Tanner hospital system. The practices and services available at the pavilion draw hundreds of patients every day.

item.content:encoded:
Hailey Realty

The Challenge

Hailey Realty requested the building of brand resources and templates for the promotion of commercial real estate properties throughout Georgia. We developed templates for flyers, brochures, offering memorandums and more.

Results

The branding has aided in the success of several property offerings. Hailey Realty continues to expand its capabilities and services in the Georgia commercial real estate market.

item.title: The Birches
item.dc:creator: wtingen
item.content:encoded:
The Birches

The Challenge

The Birches is an assisted living and memory care facility. As a new facility, they required branding and collateral to aid in the leasing of residential units. We created the branding, style guide, business collateral and promotional materials. The pieces we developed include print items, such as a booklet, a brochure, business stationery, ads and digital materials posted to social media channels and websites.

Results

The Birches opened with more than 80% of the units leased and under contract.

Advertising

Branding

Direct Mail

Logo Design

Outdoor

Photography

Print

Social Media

Video

Sales Brochure

item.dc:creator: wtingen
item.content:encoded:
Your Haven

The Challenge

A new addiction recovery organization, Your Haven, required a brand, website and collateral to help them engage the local community. We created their brand and logo. We then expanded those initial ideas into the website and print materials created for the organization.

Results

Your Haven has already helped several individuals in their community. They are also working hard to reduce the stigma many in the community feel about those suffering from addictions.

Services

Branding

Logo Design

Print

Strategy

item.title: About
item.dc:creator: wtingen
item.content:encoded:
Enhancing Brands with Creativity, Intent and Strategy

Book a call with Warren

Warren Tingen, Founder and Creative Director of Tingen Creative, has more than 20 years experience crafting brands, telling brand stories and launching marketing initiatives. His experience allows him to help hone and focus any brand's positioning and strategic goals and objectives.

Tingen Creative is ready to help you build your brand by developing the strategy and collateral necessary to take the vision you have for your business or property to the next level of success. 

Book a call with me today!

Warren Tingen, Founder and Creative Director

Client List

We are thankful and blessed to have worked with so many fantastic clients over time. Tingen Creative strives to help build robust and amazing brands at each engagement.

item.title: Seefried Industrial Properties
item.dc:creator: wtingen
item.content:encoded:
Seefried Industrial Properties

The Challenge

Seefried Industrial Properties wanted to reinforce and strengthen their brand. They asked us to aid in the consolidation of the myriad styles employed by the Atlanta and U.S. offices. We brought the components together and create a cohesive brand. We developed a style guide and templates for flyers, presentations, booklets and other print and digital collateral.

Results

Seefried Industrial Properties’ now consistent brand has enabled them to stand out and allows for more immediate recognition in their markets. The materials we developed have aided them in the development of more than 140 million square feet and the lease of more than 30 million square feet of industrial real estate.

Services

Advertising

Branding

Direct Mail

Email

Outdoor

Photo Retouching

Presentations

Print

Social Media

Tingen Creative feels like an extension of our team and has always been an absolute pleasure to work with over the years. They do an excellent job of blending client input with their own expertise to create real impact.

I highly recommend Tingen Creative for their incredible work, responsiveness, value, and ability to implement client goals while also explaining a complex and new environment to those unfamiliar with the design world. They are truly a collaborative and reliable partner.

Barbara Bennett Marketing Coordinator, Seefried Industrial Properties

item.title: ORIStruts
item.dc:creator: wtingen
item.content:encoded:
ORIStruts

The Challenge

The owner of ORIStruts reached out to us to revitalize their site when they moved to a new manufacturing location. They wanted to update their design and platform. We started with a site inventory after which we discussed the contents with the owner to determine what could be consolidated and/or expanded. Once content was confirmed we generated the structure of the site and built wireframes and comps. Upon approval, we completed the site build adding new components such as videos and a robust dealer listing.

Results

The site has enhanced the user experience, increased traffic and sales and enticed new dealers to join the ORIStrut family.

Services

Advertising

Photo Retouching

Print

Strategy

UX/UI

Video Editing

Web

item.title: Saibhreas
item.dc:creator: wtingen
item.content:encoded:
Saibhreas Capital

The Challenge

This private fund, previously Alamo Capital, wanted to rebrand for future investments and possible public applications. Discussion with the owners of this fund lead to a renaming in addition to the rebrand. The fund owner also desired to reflect their Irish heritage within the new brand. Additionally, they wanted a more "fun" icon for their Intelligence and Research reports.

Results

Through our research we found the Gaelic word for wealth — saibhreas (pronounced sigh-vris). This unique word resonated deeply with the fund's team. We also designed a stylized dara knot to further deepen the connection to heritage. For the "fun" we developed a stylized clover.

Saibhreas now has a fully realized brand identity and collateral to help draw future investors. 

Services

Brand Strategy

Brand Identity

Brand Naming 

Presentation

item.title: Apex Industrial
item.dc:creator: wtingen
item.content:encoded:
Apex Industrial

The Challenge

Apex Industrial is a group of brokers developing a new process and business to manage industrial real estate leasing, tenant and client relationships. They approached us to help craft a unique brand identity and marketing collateral to stand out and better serve clients.

They wanted a clean, lighter look for their brand to distinguish them from other industrial brokerages. We began by expanding their color palette, solidifying font choices and selecting an imagery style.

After those creative choices were approved, we crafted collateral with voluminous white space. We focused on an eye-leading hierarchy with a high readability font size. Also chunking the written content in small components for at-a-glance reading.

Results

Apex Industrial now has a full and robust brand identity and collateral that will help them stand out among other industrial brokerage firms. We were given a tight timeline but we delivered and provided everything they needs as they started this new endeavor. They have already successfully posted materials at new client properties.

Services

Branding

Brochures

Business Cards

Direct Mail

Flyers

Logo

Outdoor

Style Guide

Marketing Collateral

Style Guide

Working with Tingen Creative to brand a new company has been a wonderful experience! They helped us from start to finish to create a brand identity we truly love and are proud to share. We will continue to use Tingen Creative as we grow and expand our new company and could not recommend Tingen Creative more.

Ryan Blackburn Managing Broker

item.title: Home
item.dc:creator: wtingen
item.content:encoded:
Improve Deals, Speed ROI

Marketing and Branding Made Easy

COMMERCIAL • DEVELOPMENT • CONSTRUCTION

Book a call with Warren

We serve individuals and businesses in commercial real estate, development, and construction. We help hone and focus brands to align owner vision and customer beliefs.

Our objective with every project is to attract attention, promote engagement and provide robust solutions to challenges your property or business face. We help bring your idea to life with unique, strategic and creative solutions.

Drafting a new story requires brand strategy, a brand name and a superior brand identity. Whether we’re starting the story for a new initiative or breathing new life into the story of an experienced property we direct the brand to new heights and the next chapter.

Testimonials

Tingen Creative combines speed and creativity to deliver exactly what we need as real estate marketing professionals. After working with Warren and his team for nearly ten years, he continues to evolve and upgrade his skills to outpace the competition, making him the clear choice to come back to time and time again! Joseph KrissLeasing Director, Seefried Industrial Properties I have worked with Tingen Creative on several projects over the last two years with great success. Tingen Creative is always responsive to our requests and their insights in the creative process have been invaluable. We look forward to with Tingen Creative on our next project. Tony GimbroneVP of Sales, Beacon Communities My experience working with Tingen Creative has been great. They are easy to work with from start to finish, providing SEO optimizations to UX/UI recommendations and design work. Their responsiveness and reliability make everything run smoothly. I know they will deliver excellent work every single time. Tonya TedrickMarketing Director, KARE Featured Work Book a call with Warren

item.title: Manor Lakes
item.dc:creator: wtingen
item.content:encoded:
Manor Lakes

The Challenge

Manor Lakes is an assisted living and memory care facility. They connected with us to make their brand more cohesive and consistent. We redeveloped and aligned the branding. Then created a style guide, business collateral and promotional materials. The pieces we developed include print items, such as a booklet, a brochure, business stationery, ads and digital materials posted to social media channels and websites.

Results

Manor Lakes now has a codified brand identity increasing brand awareness and engagement. This has created better and deeper connection with their community and with potential future clients.

Services

Art Direction

Branding

Print Collateral

Style Guide

item.title: Services
item.dc:creator: wtingen
item.content:encoded:
How We Build Your Brand

When you consider the phrase — by design — you envision a plan, a plan with the purpose and desire to accomplish specific goals and objectives.

Our objective with every project is to complete it by design. We help bring your business ideas to life with unique, strategic and creative solutions.

Our designed process allows our team to develop the right plan for your business or property, focus efforts on the correct audience and craft a lasting brand.

Book a call with Warren

Phase 1

Discovery

We listen. We listen to understand your idea and dream then help you craft the vision, mission and goals of the brand we will create together.

Research

Research will center around the collection of information on similar organizations and properties, conducting interviews with the intended target audience and searching for patterns to focus and hone the brand process.

Positioning

Positioning is the foundational moment where we strategically determine how your brand will best be perceived by the desired audience. This also helps stand out from competing brands. With strategic positioning we can align your vision and how the customers regard the brand.

Book a call to start your brand!

Phase 2

Naming

Naming a property or your business is of paramount importance. It begins the story for the audience. It is here we want the connection to start for those experiencing your brand. We will craft a name that follows characteristic designed to make it resonate and memorable as well and functional across a broad array applications.

Voice

How should this brand be voiced? Fun, friendly, luxurious, sensual? During this phase, we will determine the best voice and tone to breathe life into the brand. We will identify key words that will be a brand focus. With these key words we will further develop the brand persona.

Identity

Many consider brand identity to be the logo. However, we know identity entails so much more. Our process will unearth the right elements to excited potential customers. We will help determine the unique look and feel, color palette, style of imagery, typography and more for application across print and digital experiences with your brand.

Guidelines

We craft a style guide to maintain brand consistency across all future efforts. The style guide will be our compass as we create the final pieces of the brand process.

Tactics

Based on these efforts we skillfully craft collateral. Initializing promotional pieces range from the minor to the major, including flyers, brochures, digital ads, presentation, social content, websites, video and more.

Book a call with Warren

Phase 3

Measuring Success

Success is different for each client. We want to know what success looks like for you. We address this so we can specifically aim for those targets. Our primary goal is to see you and your business succeed and thrive.

item.title: UFB
item.dc:creator: wtingen
item.content:encoded:
Unique Food and Beverage (UFB)

The Challenge

Unique Food and Beverage (UFB) had recently experienced a large amount of growth and investment funds from a partnering organization. UFB desired to polish their look, expand their website and position themselves for continued growth in the future. They contacted us to help them with their brand strategy, brand identity and website update.

We held a discovery session to review their request and any undiscovered needs. We walked their team through our brand strategy framework. We were able to identify and study several competitors and clearly define factors of differentiation. Some of these factors included the UFB team’s ability to decrease transaction times at venues through process improvements and the owner’s keen sense for where efficiencies can be created with operation layout design.

With the strategy complete we were able to quickly develop the foundational elements of the brand identity. A stylescape was developed, which consists of a mood board or imagery gallery as well as a color selection. Logo options were sketched and reviewed. The selected logo is a stylized U. The U in UFB sits within the negative space of a line signifying a queue line at an event venue.

The UFB website was expanded from its single page to a multiple page site. Our brand strategy session allowed us to add content to the site to impact SEO. Additonally, we more fully define the capabilities and offerings of UFB.

Results

The UFB brand has been improved well beyond its first stage. They were very please with our work rebranding their business for its next phase of growth.

Their brand identity now matches the clients they serve and those they will seek in the future. The website has been expanded from its single page to a multi-page site detailing the UFB services, processes and client benefits.

Shortly after the rebrand, UFB landed two new venues. More recently they added a million dollar venue.

item.title: Capital Development Partners
item.dc:creator: wtingen
item.content:encoded:
Capital Development Partners

The Challenge

Capital Development Partners (CDP) approached us to help them codify and solidify their brand. CDP is a major player in the development of industrial and shipping for ports in the southeast. Using existing brand and marketing elements, we consolidated the brand. We held robust discussions with the CDP team to arrive at the essence of the CDP brand.

After defining the true CDP brand we designed the brand identity style guide for use to maintain consistency in future marketing collateral and collaboration with other third party vendors and teams.

Once standards were set, we designed a new pitch deck for the team to use. Strict adherence to the brand standards was paramount for CDP as they begin the next chapter in successful development in the Southeast.

Results

CDP fully committed and now has a realized and codify brand identity. They are now enable to maintain a consistent look, feel and tone across all future marketing and presentation collateral.

Branding

item.title: SVN Marketing Report
item.dc:creator: wtingen
item.content:encoded:
SVN Marketing Report

The Challenge

John Bunch, SIOR reached out to me to assist with a new marketing report for his region in Kentucky. We discuss a variety of requirements and the SVN brand standard we needed to maintain for the new piece. It needed to be attractive, engaging and portable across a variety of formats and platforms.

He and his team were very clear with the direction they wanted to take the report. They provide fantastic vision for the resulting piece.

Results

We crafted a showcase report for John and the SVN team. They were able to distribute it on social media as well as printed copies for leave behinds when visiting clients. The report has been well received by industry professionals in the region.

Services

Design

Illustration

Layout

Marketing

Photo Retouching

 

I met Warren Tingen on LinkedIn. He called me to introduce himself and succinctly told me how he could help me. This guy's skill is unreal. He created the graphic and layout of this entire report. Our internal marketing team Addy Fitz, Rachel Ridd, and Hadley Carmichael worked in tandem with Warren and made this process a seamless one.

item.title: The Imperative of Returning to the Office
item.dc:creator: Admin
item.content:encoded:
A Commercial Real Estate Perspective

The global workforce underwent a seismic shift when the pandemic forced the majority to adapt to remote work. While the initial transition presented novel freedoms, the enduring reality has illuminated the irreplaceable advantages of the traditional office environment. From the vantage point of a commercial real estate executive, the bricks-and-mortar office isn’t just a space—it’s a breeding ground for growth, productivity, and unity.

Culture: The Heartbeat of the Corporation

The essence of a company’s culture lies in its unique environment. It’s challenging, if not impossible, to replicate the creative and stimulating milieu of an office in a remote setting. An office, adorned with brand colors and values, serves as a constant reminder of the company’s mission, inspiring employees to internalize and uphold its principles.

Collaboration and Teamwork: More Than Just Meetings

While virtual interactions offer convenience, they cannot replace the organic and spontaneous exchanges that occur within office walls. Whether it’s a serendipitous brainstorming session in the hallway or a quick lunch with a colleague, these encounters hone interpersonal skills and fortify team bonds. In essence, the physical space enhances communication, propelling not only individual but also collective performance.

Loyalty and Pride: Anchoring the Workforce

Offices play a pivotal role in cultivating loyalty. Regular face-to-face interactions reinforce bonds, making employees feel valued and less inclined to seek opportunities elsewhere. Moreover, firsthand recognition, especially from senior executives, instills pride and motivates employees to continually strive for excellence.

Relationships: The Cornerstone of Success

An office is more than just a workplace; it’s a nexus for networking. Interactions within the office and the broader building community foster both professional and personal relationships. Such relationships, difficult to cultivate virtually, are instrumental for long-term success.

Performance: Maximizing Potential

Offices enhance clarity, aligning employees with the company’s objectives. Sharing space with diverse talents spurs idea exchange, promoting innovation. Moreover, a dedicated workspace, devoid of home distractions, sharpens focus, driving productivity.

Diversity: Achieving Genuine Inclusivity

Achieving workforce diversity — a paramount goal in today’s business landscape — thrives in an in-person environment. Offices foster genuine understanding, appreciation, and collaboration across diverse groups, laying the foundation for enduring inclusivity.

Management: Streamlined and Effective

In-office management offers leaders clear channels for swift problem solving and immediate feedback, ensuring employees align with company goals. On-site presence aids hands-on training, allowing employees to directly gain from expert knowledge. The physical office environment also encourages cross-selling and streamlines recruitment, while promoting networking and mentorship among colleagues.

Work Life-Balance and Health: Delineating Boundaries

Data from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics highlights a decline in productivity since Q4 of 2020, coinciding with the adoption of extended remote work. As the lines between work and home blur, the importance of a designated workspace grows. A physical office not only boosts productivity but also helps delineate work from leisure, crucial for mental health and overall productivity. Modern offices, with their emphasis on wellness programs and amenities, become bastions for holistic health, aiming for a workforce that enjoys both professional success and personal well-being.

The Tangible Impact

The decision to return to the office isn’t merely about traditionalism; It’s anchored in tangible outcomes. The structured setting of an office is conducive to enhanced productivity, a factor that invariably drives company profits. This heightened efficiency and the cohesive work environment also lead to improved retention rates, ensuring a stable and committed workforce. Additionally, an office-based operation tends to be more attractive for prospective employees, streamlining the recruitment process and drawing top-tier talent. In the larger scheme of things, the physical office isn’t just a space; It’s a strategic asset with multifaceted benefits.

Commercial Properties: Adapting for a Brighter Future

As the global business landscape evolves, so does the commercial real estate sector. Office buildings, more than ever, are prioritizing the needs and well-being of their occupants, ensuring they return to a setting that’s not only conducive to work but also nourishing for the individual.

Clean Spaces: The pandemic has underscored the importance of hygiene. Modern office buildings are now championing more rigorous cleaning protocols, ensuring every workspace is sanitized to the highest standards, instilling confidence in the occupants.

Health and Fitness: Recognizing the profound impact of physical well-being on productivity and mental health, commercial properties are now home to state-of-the-art fitness facilities. Moreover, wellness programs are frequently on offer, promoting holistic health.

Networking Opportunities: Whether for business or leisure, networking remains an integral aspect of professional growth. Many office buildings are actively curating events and platforms for both social and business networking, fostering a sense of community.

Training and Community Workspaces: Adapting to the fluid nature of modern businesses, commercial spaces now offer dedicated areas for training and community projects. These flexible zones facilitate collaboration and continuous learning.

Amenities Galore: Beyond the confines of the office, the surrounding environment plays a pivotal role in enhancing the work experience. Many commercial properties are strategically situated near or even house various amenities—be it restaurants, retail shops, or recreational zones. These conveniences further enrich the daily lives of employees.

Navigating the New Workplace Norms

In the aftermath of pandemic restrictions, several leading corporations are mandating a return to office work, reflecting a belief in the potential advantages of in-person collaboration and productivity. Giants like JP Morgan Chase, Amazon, and Salesforce have updated or abandoned earlier hybrid models in favor of more regular office attendance.* JP Morgan, for instance, expects all its managing directors to be present five days a week, and Amazon’s CEO has specified that corporate staffers be in the office for at least three days weekly. Despite these shifts, reactions from employees have varied, with some showing resistance. For example, many Amazon and Apple employees voiced their concerns, with some even resorting to petitions against the new mandates. Such directives and the ensuing responses underscore the ongoing debate on the optimal balance between remote work and office presence in the post-pandemic business landscape.

As we contemplate the future of work, it’s paramount to recognize the enduring value of the physical office. It’s not just a space — it’s an ecosystem that nurtures growth, unity, and success.

References

Bernstein, Ethan, Hayley Blunden, Andrew Brodsky, Wonbin Sohn, and Ben Waber. “The Implications of Working Without an Office.” Harvard Business Review, July 15, 2020, 

https://hbr.org/2020/07/the-implications-of-working-without-an-office.

item.title: Is Commercial Real Estate Ever Coming Back?
item.dc:creator: Admin
item.content:encoded:
The Past, Present, and Future of Commercial Real Estate Market Cycles

Questions we hear all the time — 

  • Will the commercial real estate market ever come back?
  • Will employees ever be back in the office?
  • How long will this last?

Believe it or not, the Commercial Real Estate (CRE) market cycle tells a optimistic story.

Just as General MacArthur said, “I shall return,” so will the CRE markets, as they have time and time again over the past decades.

The ever-evolving world of commercial real estate (CRE) is a testament to the resilience and adaptability of markets in the face of many challenges. Over the past four decades, we’ve witnessed five significant downturns in the CRE sector, each triggered by different global events. Yet, every time the dust settled, the industry rebounded stronger. Let’s review these cycles and project into the future.

A Look Back at the CRE Down Cycles

  • 1980-82: High inflation, soaring interest rates, and the repercussions of the oil embargo rattled the global economy. Add to that the overbuilding in CRE, and it’s no surprise the sector witnessed a downturn.
  • 1990-93: The Savings and Loan (S&L) crisis culminated in the creation of the Resolution Trust Corporation (RTC). Paired with the rise of telecommuting and a major stock market drop in 1989, CRE faced a challenging landscape.
  • 2001-05: The turn of the millennium was marked by the dot-com bubble burst, followed closely by the 9/11 attacks. These events saw thousands of companies vacate their office spaces, especially in lower Manhattan.
  • 2007-10: The subprime mortgage crisis hit hard. Interestingly, while telecommuting gained momentum between 2005 and 2013, many firms that embraced full remote work models began recalling employees to offices by 2014.
  • 2022-Present: Unquestionably, the Covid-19 pandemic has brought about the most profound change in recent times. The subsequent economic fallout, coupled with rising national debts, inflation, and interest rate hikes, has created an uncertain environment for CRE.

The Present State of CRE

We are currently in the throes of a downturn catalyzed by the Covid-19 pandemic. The transition to remote work, prompted by global lockdowns, has dramatically affected CRE, particularly the office sector. The present scenario is somewhat reminiscent of the telecommuting trends that emerged in the early 2010s. However, the current situation has broader implications given its global scale and the rapid technological advances supporting remote work.

On the flip side, certain segments within CRE are thriving. Warehousing and logistics centers, for instance, are seeing an uptick due to the surge in e-commerce. Similarly, data centers are proliferating with the digital transformation wave. 

Current Landscape and Projections

Next 1 Year: The pandemic’s most significant impact has been the normalization of remote work. Companies realized the viability of remote operations, leading many to reduce their physical office spaces. While this means a short-term dip in demand, the flip side is that there’s potential for CRE to diversify. Spaces can be repurposed – think co-working spaces, warehousing for e-commerce, or mixed-use developments.

Next 5 Years: The trend of urbanization isn’t going away. Cities will continue to grow, and businesses will always need commercial spaces. However, the nature of these spaces will evolve. We’ll likely see more hybrid models where offices are used for collaborations and meetings rather than daily work. Furthermore, sustainability will be at the forefront. Green buildings, efficient energy use, and other sustainable practices will not be just an added advantage but a necessity.

Next 10 Years: A decade from now, technology will play an even bigger role in CRE. Smart buildings equipped with AI, IoT, and other cutting-edge technologies will dominate the landscape. We can expect to see more flexible spaces, catering to ever-changing business needs. The CRE sector will also need to be prepared for potential challenges – be it another global crisis or the effects of climate change.

Positives Outlooks

The very nature of downturns means that there’s room for growth afterwards. With every cycle, we’ve seen innovations in the CRE sector. The rise of co-working spaces post the 2008-12 downturn is a prime example. Additionally, as technology becomes more integrated with our spaces, there’s potential for CRE to offer solutions that we haven’t even thought of yet.

Diversification of Use: The traditional usage of commercial spaces is evolving. With the rise of the digital economy, there’s a growing demand for data centers. Similarly, the healthcare sector’s expansion might increase the demand for medical office spaces.

E-Commerce and Logistics: The continued rise of e-commerce has led to a greater demand for logistics centers, warehouses, and distribution hubs, providing a significant boost to the industrial real estate segment.

Adaptive Reuse: There’s a growing trend towards repurposing old commercial spaces for new uses, like turning outdated malls into residential complexes or entertainment hubs.

Sustainable and Green Buildings: As environmental concerns rise, the demand for sustainable and green buildings is expected to grow, opening new avenues for developers and investors.

Hybrid Work Model: Although work from home has become prevalent, a hybrid model where employees work partly from home and partly from the office is gaining traction. This model still necessitates the presence of office spaces, albeit restructured for flexibility.

Challenges Ahead for CRE

External factors like global crises or economic downturns will always loom over the industry. There’s also the challenge of keeping up with rapidly changing business needs. While technology presents opportunities, it also poses threats. 

Technological Disruptions: The rapid pace of technological advancement can lead to unforeseen challenges. For instance, the rise of virtual reality could change the way retail or office spaces are conceptualized.

Remote Work: The rise of remote work can lead to reduced demand for traditional office spaces. Companies might opt for smaller offices or co-working spaces, affecting the demand dynamics of the sector.

Economic Volatility: With concerns about national debt, inflation, and interest rates, the economic environment remains uncertain. Economic downturns typically result in reduced demand for commercial spaces, at least in the short term.

Overbuilding: Historically, periods of prosperity in CRE have sometimes led to overbuilding, creating a supply-demand mismatch.

Conclusion

History has shown us that the CRE industry is adaptable and resilient. While the challenges faced in each cycle differ, the sector’s ability to adapt and innovate remains constant. As the industry navigates the post-pandemic world, it’s equipped with lessons from the past and a vision for the future.

References

DeLuca, Marc. 2022. “What History Teaches Us About Inflation And Commercial Real Estate.” Forbes Business Council, July 18, 2022. https://www.forbes.com/sites/forbesbusinesscouncil/2022/07/18/what-history-teaches-us-about-inflation-and-commercial-real-estate/?sh=6e38c0554d52.

Morgan, Brady. 2023. “The Future Of Global Remote Work: Navigating A New Landscape.” Forbes Business Council, May 30, 2023. https://www.forbes.com/sites/forbesbusinesscouncil/2023/05/30/the-future-of-global-remote-work-navigating-a-new-landscape/?sh=53331ee05d30.

Tasman, Gary. 2022. “What Smart Buildings Could Mean for the Future.” NAIOP, August 29, 2022. https://blog.naiop.org/2022/08/what-smart-buildings-could-mean-for-the-future/#:~:text=This%20means%20the%20building%20can,buildings%20may%20become%20smart%20buildings.

item.title: Networking in 2030: How AI Will Change How We Connect
item.dc:creator: Admin
item.content:encoded:
As we approach 2030, artificial intelligence (AI) is poised to revolutionize networking within the real estate sector, transforming how professionals connect, collaborate, and conduct business. This evolution presents both opportunities and challenges for real estate professionals, developers, and marketers.​

AI-Driven Networking Platforms

Traditional networking methods are giving way to AI-powered platforms that facilitate more efficient and targeted connections. These platforms analyze vast amounts of data to recommend contacts, predict networking opportunities, and personalize interactions. For instance, AI can match real estate professionals with potential investors or partners based on shared interests and goals, streamlining the networking process.​

Enhanced Communication Tools

AI is enhancing communication through tools like chatbots and virtual assistants, enabling real-time, personalized interactions. These technologies can handle routine inquiries, schedule meetings, and provide instant responses, allowing professionals to focus on more strategic tasks. Such advancements lead to increased productivity and improved client satisfaction.​

Predictive Analytics for Market Insights

Networking in 2030 will heavily rely on AI-driven predictive analytics to gain deeper market insights. By analyzing trends and consumer behavior, AI can identify emerging opportunities and potential risks, enabling professionals to make informed decisions. This data-centric approach fosters more meaningful connections and collaborations within the industry.​

Virtual and Augmented Reality Networking

The integration of AI with virtual and augmented reality is set to redefine networking experiences. Virtual conferences, property tours, and interactive meetings will become commonplace, allowing professionals to connect globally without geographical constraints. This technological fusion offers immersive experiences, enhancing engagement and collaboration.​

Ethical Considerations and Data Privacy

As AI becomes integral to networking, ethical considerations and data privacy will be paramount. Professionals must navigate the balance between leveraging data for networking advantages and respecting privacy laws and ethical standards. Establishing transparent data practices and obtaining informed consent will be crucial to maintaining trust and compliance.​wsj.com

Adapting to the AI-Driven Networking Landscape

To thrive in this evolving landscape, real estate professionals should embrace continuous learning and adaptability. Staying updated on AI advancements, investing in relevant technologies, and developing digital literacy will be essential. Building a robust online presence and engaging with AI-driven platforms can enhance visibility and networking effectiveness.​Todo sobre IA

In conclusion, AI is set to transform networking in the real estate industry by 2030, offering enhanced connectivity, efficiency, and insights. Embracing these changes proactively will position professionals to capitalize on new opportunities and navigate the challenges of an AI-driven networking environment.

item.title: SVN Knoxville Report
item.dc:creator: wtingen
item.content:encoded:
SVN Knoxville Report

The Challenge

Matthew Strother contacted  me to help his team with a marketing report for his region in Knoxville. He and his team were very clear with the direction they wanted to take the report and how they wanted to present it. The report was to be created to be both digital and printable in format. The SVN team expects to generate excitement about the region's prospects and opportunities. 

Results

This special market report was created to help Matthew and his team in Knoxville showcase their knowledge and understand of the local market. They've forwarded the report to clients and other individuals with interest in the Knoxville area. They expect to update and use the report quarter after quarter.

Services

Design

Illustration

Layout

item.title: Horizon Living
item.dc:creator: wtingen
item.content:encoded:
Horizon Living

The Challenge

Manor Lake Development was preparing a new service in senior living. They are creating a new senior community focused on Independent Living for the 55+ individuals and couples. They initially contacted me to create a new brand. After discovery conversations, we recognized that a brand extension rather than a new brand was the path to success. We decided to design an identity that maintained elements of the Manor Lake brand identity and expand upon it. We also created a variety of marketing materials to aid in the promotion of the Horizon Independent Living Community.

Results

This brand extension will serve to elevate this new service line in the first of many such planned developments under the Manor Lake umbrella. The owner and management team appreciated the speed and clarity we brought to the process. 

Services

Brand Identity Design

Illustration

Layout

Marketing

Photo Retouching

Working with Warren and the team at Tingen Creative was a seamless experience from start to finish. We came to them with a vision for branding our newest independent living development, Horizon, and they delivered quickly and efficiently. The final logo and marketing materials captured the essence of what we were building—freedom, comfort, and community for active seniors. Warren asked the right questions, listened closely, and made the process feel collaborative and efficient. We had a tight timeline, but their professionalism and creative clarity made it easy. We’re thrilled with the results and wouldn’t hesitate to work with them again.

Samantha Lee, LPN, CEA, CALA Vice President of Operations for Manor Lake Management

item.title: dress gray
item.dc:creator: wtingen
item.content:encoded:
dress gray

The Challenge

dress gray contacted me to help them establish their brand in construction management and development. They were already working under the dress gray moniker. However, they hadn't yet clear defined who they were serving, why it was important and how they were different than other construction management firms in the industry.

We began with a Discovery Session where we unearthed what the owner and other stakeholders have already accomplished and how they wanted the dress gray brand to move forward. This was followed by our Strategy Workshop to help us identify the right audience to sharpen the dress gray focus, to clear define what and how dress gray presents to current and potential clients. As part of our Strategy Workshop we interviewed clients to understand how the audience perceived dress gray. Through these methods we gathers a wealth of information to help us clearly make dress gray stand out and succeed.

Only after these processes did we dive into crafting the verbal and visual expression of the dress gray brand. After completed these elements we created a variety of templates to aid in proposals and promotion of the brand.

Results

dress gray is well on its way to successful engagements with many clients. After completion of this process the owner informed us of two engagement in the works and another proposal just sent out. dress gray is well on its way to establish itself as an amazing construction management and development company.

Services

Brand Strategy

Brand Identity Design

Discovery

Illustration

Interviews

Marketing

Photo Management

Research

item.title: How the New Trump Administration Could Impact the Housing Real Estate Market
item.dc:creator: Admin
item.content:encoded:
As a new administration takes office, policy shifts could significantly influence the U.S. housing market. 

The Trump administration has outlined several proposals, ranging from regulatory reform to changes in immigration and mortgage policies, all of which could have far-reaching effects on housing affordability, supply and market stability.

Regulatory Reforms and Housing Supply

The Trump administration aims to reduce regulations affecting housing construction. President-elect Trump has noted that regulatory costs account for about 30% of the price of a new home. His administration plans to cut these costs and open portions of federal land for large-scale housing construction. 

If implemented effectively, these reforms could lower building expenses, increase the housing supply, and address affordability issues.

Immigration Policies and Construction Labor

Proposals to tighten immigration laws and deport undocumented immigrants could lead to labor shortages in the construction industry. Immigrants make up about 30% of the U.S. construction workforce, and a decrease in available labor could drive up costs for builders and slow down new housing developments. This could counteract efforts to increase the housing supply and exacerbate affordability challenges.

Mortgage Rates and Financial Markets

The administration’s economic agenda, including proposed tax cuts and increased infrastructure spending, could lead to higher inflation and government debt. These factors may result in higher mortgage rates, which have already been on the rise. 

Higher rates could make it harder for first-time buyers to enter the market and deter current homeowners from selling, slowing the overall housing market.

Affordable Housing Initiatives

To address housing affordability, the administration plans to make federal land available for development and reduce construction costs through deregulation. While these efforts could alleviate the housing shortage, their success depends on implementation and whether designated federal lands are in areas of high demand.

Potential Privatization of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac

Republicans have long advocated for the privatization of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, two critical entities in the U.S. mortgage market. Privatization aims to reduce government oversight and taxpayer risk but could lead to higher borrowing costs for homebuyers. 

This shift may have a particularly significant impact on low- and middle-income families seeking affordable financing options.

What to Expect Moving Forward

The Trump administration’s policies could bring both opportunities and challenges to the housing market. While regulatory reforms and increased land availability might boost supply, labor shortages and rising mortgage rates could hinder affordability and development. 

Also, the privatization of key mortgage institutions could reshape the housing finance landscape.

Stakeholders in the real estate industry should closely monitor these policy changes to anticipate market trends and adapt accordingly.

What do you think?

How do you see these potential policies shaping your local housing market?

item.title: What Are People Looking for in Commercial Real Estate Today?
item.dc:creator: Admin
item.content:encoded:
The commercial real estate (CRE) landscape is evolving rapidly as businesses adapt to new ways of working and living. Whether it’s office spaces, retail locations, or mixed-use developments, today’s tenants and buyers have new priorities. 

What’s trending in CRE right now?

Prime Locations Still Reign Supreme

Location remains a top consideration — but with a twist. 

Today’s tenants seek properties in vibrant, walkable neighborhoods with proximity to key amenities. Areas near public transportation hubs, major highways or airports are particularly attractive, as businesses aim to enhance employee convenience and client accessibility.

Proximity to Dining and Entertainment

The post-pandemic era has highlighted the importance of amenities like restaurants, coffee shops and entertainment venues. Tenants want spaces where employees can easily grab lunch or unwind after work, creating a more engaging environment that supports work-life balance.

Flexibility is Non-Negotiable

The rise of hybrid work has made flexibility a must. Businesses are looking for adaptable office layouts, co-working spaces and properties that can accommodate both in-person collaboration and remote work setups. 

For retail and industrial spaces, flexibility in zoning and multi-use potential is increasingly sought after.

Sustainability Matters More Than Ever

Energy-efficient buildings, green certifications and sustainable materials are in high demand. Tenants and investors are prioritizing properties that align with ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) goals, as sustainability becomes a key driver of business success.

Technology and Connectivity

From smart building systems to high-speed internet, technological infrastructure is a critical factor. Tenants expect seamless connectivity and tech-forward spaces that support productivity and innovation.

The Bottom Line

Today’s CRE market is all about accessibility, flexibility, and experience. Properties that cater to these evolving demands are poised to stand out in a competitive market.

Ready to position your listings to meet these trends? Our team specializes in marketing commercial properties that align with modern tenant and buyer needs. Let’s connect!

item.title: The Advantages and Risks of Subleasing Commercial Space During the Holidays
item.dc:creator: Admin
item.content:encoded:
The holiday season often brings unique opportunities for businesses and landlords in the commercial real estate market. Subleasing commercial space during this period can be a smart move, but it comes with both risks and rewards. Here’s a closer look at the potential benefits and challenges.

Advantages of Subleasing During the Holidays

🎁 Boosting Cash Flow

For companies with unused office or retail space, subleasing can generate extra income during a time when costs like bonuses and year-end expenses may strain budgets.

📈 Meeting Seasonal Demand

Short-term tenants — such as pop-up shops or seasonal businesses — often seek temporary spaces during the holidays, creating a surge in demand for subleases.

🌟 Building Relationships

Subleasing can foster relationships with businesses that might become long-term tenants or partners.

Risks of Holiday Subleasing

❄️ Temporary Tenants

Short-term leases carry the risk of tenant turnover and the associated administrative burden of re-leasing the space.

🔧 Wear and Tear

Increased foot traffic during the busy holiday season can lead to greater wear and tear, increasing maintenance costs.

📋 Lease Compliance Issues

Some primary lease agreements restrict subleasing, creating legal or financial risks if the process isn’t carefully managed.

Best Practices for Subleasing

  • Screen Tenants Carefully: Vet potential subtenants for financial stability and reputation to avoid future headaches.
  • Check Lease Terms: Ensure subleasing complies with your primary lease to avoid penalties.
  • Draft a Clear Sublease Agreement: Outline responsibilities, costs, and expectations to protect both parties.
  • Prepare for a Quick Turnaround: Be ready to market and finalize agreements quickly to take advantage of holiday demand.

The Bottom Line

Subleasing during the holidays can provide significant financial and strategic advantages, but only when approached carefully. By understanding the risks and following best practices, landlords and tenants can make the most of this seasonal opportunity.

✨ Are you considering subleasing your commercial space this season? Let’s discuss how to navigate the market effectively.

item.title: What are we going to do with a million obsolete office buildings?
item.dc:creator: Admin
item.content:encoded:
Just as history has seen the reinvention of great inventions that changed our lives, the world of real estate is on the brink of a similar transformation. Consider the impact of groundbreaking inventions like the printing press, which revolutionized information dissemination, or the steam engine, which altered transportation and industry. The light bulb, telephone, aeroplane, personal computer, the Internet, and the mobile phone – each of these inventions evolved over time, significantly altering our way of life.

Today, a similar evolution is unfolding in the realm of commercial real estate. Office buildings, once symbols of corporate prowess, now face a period of obsolescence, challenging us to reimagine their role in our urban landscapes. It's time for these structures to undergo their own reinvention. The following thoughts, ideas, and concepts explore how obsolete office buildings can transform, much like the great inventions of the past, to make a meaningful impact in today's marketplace.

Housing (multi-family, senior living, affordable housing, student housing, homeless shelter) is the number one talked about conversion. It shouldn’t be the sole consideration when giving new life to an obsolete property. We asked commercial real estate (CRE) experts for other possible conversion concepts. Here is a list of innovative ideas from our respondents:

  • Medical Office
  • Life sciences / Laboratories
  • Educational facility (private schools) 
  • Self-storage
  • Recording studio
  • Media production studio 
  • Permanent filming location site
  • Training Centers / Learning center
  • Workshop
  • Dojo / Gymnasium
  • Theme / Specialty centers 
  • Youth Detention Facility
  • Cannabis / Cultivation, Retail, Testing 
  • Data Center 
  • Law enforcement / firefighter training facility
  • Library
  • Legal center

The Rise of Residential Conversions

A growing trend is the transformation of office spaces into residential units. This conversion is about creating living spaces encompassing a variety of forms such as multi-family housing, senior living facilities, student accommodations, and even affordable housing. Such conversions are particularly beneficial in urban areas, where the demand for housing often exceeds supply.

The Biden-Harris Administration introduced measures to facilitate the conversion of high-vacancy commercial properties to residential use. This includes new financing options, and technical assistance, aimed at creating affordable, energy-efficient housing. These actions are part of the White House Housing Supply Action Plan, which focuses on lowering housing costs and boosting supply.

Office vacancies averaged a 40-year high at 19.6% at the end of 2023, emphasizing the need for such initiatives. The push towards conversions is backed by the potential to add significant housing units. Research suggests that 15% of commercial district office buildings in major U.S. cities are suitable for residential conversion, potentially adding around 171,470 units.

The conversion of office spaces to residential units is often seen as a solution to revitalizing downtown areas. However, it's important to understand that while office-to-residential conversions can be beneficial in certain circumstances, they are not a panacea for all challenges faced by downtown areas. Office space utilization, despite the rise in remote work, still shows signs of recovery in certain markets. The complexity and cost of conversions often require significant public funding and support to be viable.

Specialized Spaces: Tailoring to Community Needs

Specialty conversions are gaining traction, catering to specific community needs. This includes spaces for children, seniors, fitness, healthcare, wellness, and professional services. Such specialized facilities offer a unique blend of convenience and tailored services, fostering community engagement and support.

Mixed-use developments are increasingly being recognized as more beneficial than solely residential conversions. The idea of converting office spaces to a range of uses, including coworking spaces, educational facilities, and entertainment venues, can bring more vibrancy and diversity to downtown areas. This multifaceted approach aligns with the evolving nature of work and urban life, enhancing the dynamism of city centers.

Retail Revival: Transforming Office Spaces into Marketplaces

The conversion of office buildings into retail spaces marks a significant evolution in urban land use. By transforming these areas into bustling marketplaces, cities are not only filling underused spaces but also enhancing the local shopping experience. These new retail destinations, ranging from boutiques to larger department stores, are becoming integral parts of the community fabric, offering residents and visitors alike a diverse range of shopping options. This shift is revitalizing neighborhoods, stimulating local economies, and reshaping the way we think about urban retail environments.

Medical and Wellness Centers: Fostering Health in Urban Hearts

Converting spaces into medical and wellness centers is a pivotal development in urban health infrastructure. These conversions are more than just a change in building use; they represent an investment in community health and well-being. By situating medical facilities, clinics, and wellness centers in previously vacant office buildings, cities are making healthcare services more accessible and convenient. This not only addresses critical healthcare needs but also promotes a holistic approach to wellness, integrating these vital services into the daily lives of urban dwellers.

Life Sciences and Laboratories: Pioneering New Frontiers

Dedicated spaces for life sciences and laboratories represent a groundbreaking shift in the use of former office buildings. These conversions are not just about repurposing space; they are about creating foundations for scientific breakthroughs and medical advancements. By facilitating research and development in accessible urban centers, these new labs can attract top talent, foster collaboration between academia and industry, and drive innovation in crucial fields such as biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, and environmental sciences. This trend underscores the versatility of office spaces and their potential to become key players in the global pursuit of knowledge and discovery.

Nurturing Innovation: Incubating Tech and Academic Growth

Former office buildings are now emerging as epicenters for technological innovation and academic pursuit. These spaces, once defined by corporate structure, are being creatively repurposed to nurture tech startups and educational ventures. Such environments are ideal for fostering a culture of innovation, providing budding entrepreneurs and students with the resources and space to collaborate, experiment, and drive technological progress. This shift is not just about changing physical spaces; it's about fostering a new generation of thinkers and creators, turning what were once office blocks into thriving hubs of knowledge and innovation.

Elevating Entertainment: Crafting Spaces for Joy and Engagement

The transformation of office spaces into entertainment venues opens exciting opportunities for urban areas. By converting these spaces into theaters, gaming zones, or live performance stages, cities can create new cultural focal points that attract diverse crowds and bolster the local economy. This renaissance in urban entertainment not only diversifies the cityscape but also addresses the growing demand for interactive and engaging leisure activities, contributing to the vibrancy and dynamism of city life.

Challenges and Considerations

While the potential for office space conversions is vast, it's crucial to acknowledge the complexities involved. Factors such as building regulations, structural limitations, and financial feasibility play a significant role in determining the success of these conversions. Collaborations with architects, urban planners, and financial experts are key to navigating these challenges.

The decision to convert office spaces into other uses involves several considerations, including the impact on local government revenues. It's vital to balance the need for residential spaces with the preservation of commercial property tax revenues, which are significant for many cities. This delicate balancing act is essential for maintaining fiscal stability while revitalizing urban centers.

Additionally, all new developments have a team. A team capable in that category. In conversion, the team is exponentially more important. This team needs specialists and experts with experience targeted to the conversion type. These should be experts in the fields of architecture, legal, construction, brokerage, marketing, research, capital resources. They will assure the correct planning is conducted, costs are budgeted, and issues identified before and during the conversion process. The old saying, “you need all your ducks in a row,” comes to mind, before you move forward with your concept.

The Impact on Cities and Communities

The conversion of office spaces is more than a real estate trend; it's a catalyst for urban renewal and community development. These transformations can breathe new life into declining urban areas, creating vibrant, multi-use spaces that serve a variety of community needs.

While office-to-residential conversions can contribute to solving housing shortages in urban areas, they should be viewed as part of a broader strategy. This includes incentivizing new constructions and conversions equally, ensuring that public subsidies are tied to tangible public benefits, and considering the impacts on city finances and the local economy.

Conclusion: A Future of Possibilities

The evolving landscape of office space conversions is a testament to the adaptability and resilience of the real estate sector. By reimagining these spaces, we open doors to new opportunities, meeting the changing needs of our societies and economies. As we continue to navigate this terrain, the possibilities are as limitless as our collective imagination.
